description: French composer who loosened functional harmony in favor of color, atmosphere, and timbre. His piano music evokes images through static, sensuous sonorities rather than goal-directed progressions.
harmonic_language: Non-functional harmony: parallel chords (planing) of triads, sevenths and ninths; whole-tone and pentatonic scales; modal inflections; unresolved dissonances treated as color; ambiguous, suspended tonality.
style_notes: Move chords in parallel motion (planing) — slide whole sonorities up and down rather than resolving each voice functionally.
Use the whole-tone scale, pentatonic figures, and church modes to blur the sense of a home key.
Favor static harmony: dwell on a colorful chord, often over a pedal point, rather than driving toward cadences.
Texture is layered and atmospheric: shimmering arpeggiated figuration, soft repeated chords, washes of pedal-blurred sound.
Dynamics stay mostly soft (pp - mp) with subtle swells; climaxes are rare and quickly subside.
Rhythm is fluid and unmetered in feel — avoid heavy downbeats; let phrases float without strong accent.
